raw_response:
I'm 60 years old, been working these fields since I was 20. Never went to school — can't read those papers the extension office hands out — but I know my land. My old man and me farm our 16.9 mu. Our children are in Shijiazhuang working factory jobs; they send a little money home, but not much. We can't rely on it.

This year I'm keeping things the same. Change is risky. I've got about 10 mu in wheat-maize, 4 mu in cotton, and the rest — about 3 mu — in chili. I don't put all my eggs in one basket. If the worms eat the cotton, at least I still have the grain. If the chili price crashes, I still have wheat to make flour.

**Wheat** is already in the ground from last October. It looks okay so far, not great. In March when it greened up, I put about 20 jin of urea on each mu — same as my neighbor Aunt Li. I don't measure fancy, just two big scoops per mu. I'll water it one more time before harvest if the rain doesn't come. The custom combine comes in early June. Costs 50 yuan per mu, but we're too old to cut it by hand anymore. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu. If I get the same this year, I'll be happy.

**Maize** goes in right after the wheat comes off — June 10th or 12th, very quick. Sometimes we only have five or six days. I buy hybrid seed from Old Wang's shop, about 4 jin per mu. Costs more than saving your own seed, but you get more grain. I put one bag of compound fertilizer in the hole at planting — one bag per mu, same as always. When the maize is knee-high, I topdress with another scoop of urea. Water it once, maybe twice if it's dry. Harvest late September. I hope for 1,000 jin per mu, but you never know with the weather.

**Cotton** I'm planting now, late April. First I plow and make the rows, then lay the plastic film to keep it warm. I put about half a bag of compound fertilizer in the furrows — cotton doesn't like too much nitrogen or it just grows tall leaves and no bolls. I water three times: once at planting, once when it flowers, and once when the bolls are swelling. The big worry is the bollworm. I spray bug medicine four or five times over the summer. It's a lot of work, especially the picking in September and October. My back hurts for weeks, but what can you do? We pick it ourselves. I expect about 500–600 jin of seed cotton per mu if the worms don't come.

**Chili** — I bought seedlings from the market last week. I'll transplant them in early May. I put chicken manure and some compound fertilizer in the beds first. Chili needs water but not waterlogged, so I water carefully — maybe four times through the summer. I also spray for bugs and that white mold. Picking starts in July and goes until October, every few days when they turn red. It's small money but steady.

Money is always tight. I have about 5,500 yuan to spend on all the inputs this year. If I buy too much fertilizer, I might not have cash left if one of us gets sick and needs medicine. So I use a bit less than what the rich business farms use. Better to waste a little yield than to have no money in my pocket. I've farmed this way for 40 years. It won't make me rich, but it keeps food on the table.
